adversary_position: Malicious user or system designer controlling role/system prompts.
adversary_capabilities: Inject template or Red–Blue-generated role-specific prompts; no model-weight or framework-code control.
preconditions: Role prompts are configurable and outputs are exchanged during collaboration.
mechanism: Role-conditioned prompt attack generated through Red–Blue interaction.
interaction_surface: Role prompts; system prompts; inter-agent dialogue; downstream review/filter.
primary_system_failure: Collaborative safety/output-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Higher harmful/non-refusal generation in tested agent systems than selected isolated-model baselines; no environment-side action is verified.
metric_definition: Harmful-output and non-refusal attack-success measures.
unit_denominator: Prompt/query examples per framework/configuration; the paper’s ASR is an output-classification measure, not affected-agent fraction.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Sec. 4 p. 5 setup; p. 6 Tables 2-3 for interaction and quantity comparisons; Secs. 3-4 Figs. 2-4 for EG and target settings.

adversary_position: External adversary seeds one selected agent with one adversarial image.
adversary_capabilities: Seeds the initial memory item; no continued intervention is required under the modeled propagation process.
preconditions: Agents retrieve memory content and exchange it through randomized pairwise chats.
mechanism: Memory seeding followed by retention and retransmission of the adversarial behavior.
interaction_surface: Agent memory; pairwise inter-agent communication.
primary_system_failure: F1 compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Population-level harmful or unaligned behavior. The one-million figure is simulated scale, not deployed prevalence.
metric_definition: Infected population and propagation behavior over interaction rounds.
unit_denominator: Unit: Agent and population.; Denominator: Population size, with infection status defined by the paper.
evidence_locators: Official PMLR abstract and paper record; paper Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1 to 2; threat formulation and propagation analysis, PDF pp. 1 to 3.

adversary_position: Malicious member/participant in a debate group.
adversary_capabilities: Chooses an incorrect answer and generates persuasive arguments visible to peer agents; inference-time persuasion optimization.
preconditions: Debate architecture with shared responses; at least one malicious participant; aggregate majority decision.
mechanism: Persuasion-driven adversarial debate and collective influence.
interaction_surface: Coordination/debate; inter-agent messages; aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision integrity failure.
reported_impact: System and individual accuracy drops; increased agreement with the adversary.
metric_definition: Majority Vote Accuracy and Adversary Agreement, plus individual/group accuracy change from initial to final round.
unit_denominator: Question-level proportions over benchmark items; not per-agent or per-message ASR.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-2 for setup and headline effects; Sec. 3 pp. 3-4; Sec. 4 pp. 4-7; Fig. 6-7 pp. 7-8; conclusion p. 8.

adversary_position: Malicious user and/or system designer modifying human input or agent role/system prompts.
adversary_capabilities: Injects dark-trait prompts at the human-input interface or into one or more agent role prompts; may repeat input attacks across rounds.
preconditions: Role-conditioned LLM agents; access to user input or agent system prompts; agents exchange outputs over one or more rounds.
mechanism: Dark-trait/role prompt injection, human-input attack, and hybrid repeated injection causing dangerous behavior during interaction.
interaction_surface: Human input; role/system prompt; inter-agent dialogue.
primary_system_failure: Collective safety and decision-integrity degradation; not a clean confidentiality/authorization attack.
reported_impact: Dangerous outputs during safe and dangerous tasks, including process-level and joint collective danger.
metric_definition: Process Danger Rate (at least one dangerous agent behavior in a problem/round process), Joint Danger Rate by round (all agent behaviors dangerous), plus psychological score.
unit_denominator: PDR/JDR are proportions over problem instances; JDR is round-specific. They are not conventional task-level ASR.
evidence_locators: ACL PDF pp. 1-4, Secs. 2.2-2.4; p. 4 Secs. 3.1-3.3; pp. 6-8 Tables 3-5; Appendix B p. 14 for PDR/JDR definitions.

adversary_position: Two or more colluding agents communicating under an observer or monitor.
adversary_capabilities: Generate overt messages, encode and decode hidden payloads, and coordinate on a code or strategy.
preconditions: The observer sees overt traffic but lacks complete access to private knowledge, shared intent, or the covert code.
mechanism: Steganographic encoding embedded in apparently innocuous communication.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent communication; shared implicit knowledge; observer boundary.
primary_system_failure: Oversight or monitorability integrity failure at claim level.
reported_impact: Can also produce confidentiality loss or collective-decision corruption depending on the scenario. It should not be forced into one universal impact category.
metric_definition: Coordination success, covert communication success, detectability, task performance, and scenario-specific secrecy or coupling measures.
unit_denominator: Unit: Communication episode, group, or task depending on experiment.; Denominator: Experiment-specific trials; there is no single paper-wide ASR denominator.
evidence_locators: Abstract, PDF p. 1; definition and threat model in Sec. 3.1, approximately PDF p. 4; monitor and decentralized-AI setting in Sec. 4; empirical metrics and evaluations in Secs. 5 and 6; mitigation discussion in Sec. 7.

adversary_position: External white-box adversary controlling/perturbing the first agent’s multimodal input.
adversary_capabilities: Gradient and sampling access; optimize image/audio perturbation through the wolf-to-sheep composition.
preconditions: Workflow forwards generated text and perturbed media from first MLLM to second; white-box access to composed models.
mechanism: Projected-gradient cross-agent multimodal injection through a wolf operative.
interaction_surface: Multimodal input; forwarded media; inter-agent prompt.
primary_system_failure: Downstream agent safety/output-integrity failure.
reported_impact: A clean recipient emits targeted prohibited content; onward reproduction or population spread is not demonstrated.
metric_definition: Manually judged attack-success rate and transferability across 14 prohibited-content scenarios.
unit_denominator: Scenario/trial outputs; the note flags an unresolved printed trial denominator that requires final PDF confirmation.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Sec. 3 p. 3 Eq. 2/Fig. 2; Sec. 4 pp. 4-5 Table 1/Figs. 2-4.

adversary_position: One malicious member or troublemaker agent.
adversary_capabilities: Injects optimized retrieval and replication suffixes into messages or memory content that honest agents later retrieve and retransmit.
preconditions: Agents maintain independent memories and store and retrieve interaction content.
mechanism: Adversarial retrieval and replication optimization creates a contagious jailbreak.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent messages; independent agent memories; communication topology.
primary_system_failure: F1 compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Population-wide jailbreak among previously honest agents.
metric_definition: ASR by round, maximum ASR over rounds, and rounds to reach a target ASR.
unit_denominator: Unit: Agent-question pair and interaction round.; Denominator: The paper defines the round metric over agent by question cases, then reports the maximum over rounds for its summary ASR.
evidence_locators: Abstract, PDF p. 1; metric definition in Sec. 2.2, approximately PDF p. 3; experiment tables for topology and large-scale settings; abstract and result tables for the reported improvements.

adversary_position: Internal/source-side attacker with ability to inject through an initial agent and partial topology/defense knowledge.
adversary_capabilities: Partitions and routes adversarial prompt chunks, knows target architecture and partial network/safety placement, optimizes prompt tokens.
preconditions: Graph-modeled LLM network, chunk accumulation at target memory, edge token budgets and variable arrival order, target model known.
mechanism: Minimum-cost maximum-flow route selection plus permutation-invariant adversarial prompt optimization.
interaction_surface: Communication topology; message chunks; edge safety filters; target memory/context.
primary_system_failure: Target-agent safety/instruction integrity failure; graph-mediated jailbreak. Population compromise is not directly measured.
reported_impact: Harmful target output and defense-evasion; topology affects ASR.
metric_definition: ASR over harmful prompts after one sampled chunk permutation, reported as min/mean/max across three random-topology trials; detector F1 for safety mechanisms.
unit_denominator: Prompt/test-case level across JailbreakBench, AdversarialBench, and in-the-wild jailbreak sets; not population infection.
evidence_locators: PDF Sec. 3 pp. 3-4; Sec. 4 pp. 4-5; Table 1 pp. 5-6; Secs. 5.2-5.4 pp. 6-8; Appendix B pp. 12-13.

adversary_position: Unauthorized or impersonating member agent; malicious writer to shared memory.
adversary_capabilities: Request protected information, present false authority, or write poisoned content to shared memory.
preconditions: Agents and information are assigned hierarchical security labels; ThreatSieve and HierarCache are trusted enforcement components.
mechanism: Authority-aware message filtering and hierarchical memory management are tested against unauthorized requests, impersonation, and poisoning.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent communication; identity/authority metadata; shared memory.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and shared-state integrity failure.
reported_impact: Unauthorized disclosure or downstream influence from poisoned memory in the evaluated scenarios.
metric_definition: Defense success rate under adversarial scenarios, task utility, and scalability measures.
unit_denominator: Attack-scenario/trial level; the abstract’s “above 80%” is an aggregate defense success statement, not a universal guarantee.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for two-component design and >80% headline; paper Sec. 3 framework and Sec. 4 experiments. Exact table/page locators require author signoff against v2 PDF.

adversary_position: Adversarial or persistently unreliable member agents in iterative question answering.
adversary_capabilities: Submit misleading answers/contributions through the normal collaboration protocol.
preconditions: Agent identity persists across queries; past contribution quality can be scored; the credibility updater and aggregator are trusted.
mechanism: Historical credibility scores attenuate the influence of agents whose prior contributions were judged poor.
interaction_surface: Member contributions; identity/history state; collective aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity failure under adversarial member influence.
reported_impact: Reduced answer accuracy under adversarial populations and empirical recovery from credibility-weighted aggregation.
metric_definition: Final task accuracy/robustness by adversarial population ratio; credibility values and related ablations.
unit_denominator: Question/task-instance level aggregated over experimental sets. “Adversary-majority” is an empirical task-accuracy condition, not Byzantine agreement.
evidence_locators: ACL Anthology metadata and abstract; published PDF Secs. 2–4 for scoring, Sec. 5/results tables for adversarial ratios. Exact table locators require author signoff.

adversary_position: Insider or party with one-time/continuous write access to shared generated code.
adversary_capabilities: Insert exfiltration function, obfuscate it, and add misleading comments or poisoned few-shot examples.
preconditions: Writable shared code store; downstream agents trust and inspect the artifact; success means malicious function remains in final code.
mechanism: Shared-artifact code injection and natural-language reviewer poisoning.
interaction_surface: Shared code artifact; review comments; cross-stage software workflow.
primary_system_failure: Software artifact integrity failure; potential confidentiality impact.
reported_impact: Final output retains an exfiltration function; actual data exfiltration is potential rather than executed against a real system.
metric_definition: Pass@1, attack effectiveness, model calls, and reviewer/security-agent detection outcomes.
unit_denominator: HumanEval’s 164 tasks, with three trials; attack-effectiveness percentages are task/trial based, not agent compromise rates.
evidence_locators: Full text Secs. 4-5 pp. 3-4, Fig. 1 and Listing 1; Secs. 5.3-6 p. 4; Sec. 7 pp. 5-6 Table III; Sec. 8 p. 6.

adversary_position: Colluding member agents sharing a covert textual scheme.
adversary_capabilities: Encode coordination signals in ordinary messages and adapt behavior to the allowed channel.
preconditions: Auditor can observe transcripts/outcomes and perform paired interventions, paraphrasing, rate limits, or role permutations; some fairness analysis assumes subgroup labels.
mechanism: Paired-run KL and mutual-information diagnostics, permutation/watermark/fairness signals, and calibrated union testing detect or constrain collusion.
interaction_surface: Natural-language communication; auditor intervention; outcome/fairness signals.
primary_system_failure: Oversight and collective-decision integrity failure through steganographic collusion.
reported_impact: Detection power and false-positive-controlled auditing on ColludeBench and external collusion suites; not universal detectability.
metric_definition: Detection power at a fixed 10^-3 false-positive budget, mutual-information/KL diagnostics, permutation invariance, watermark variance, fairness-aware acceptance bias, and e-value calibration.
unit_denominator: Run- or paired-run level over benchmark scenarios, including 10,000 honest runs for calibration according to the abstract.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for contributions, 10^-3 FPR, 10k honest runs, and external-suite evaluation; paper Secs. 5–6 and results/limitations for benchmark and detectors. Exact pages/tables require author signoff.

adversary_position: Byzantine or Sybil member, message/prompt tamperer, or compromised protocol participant.
adversary_capabilities: Spoof identity, equivocate, tamper with task messages/state, abuse delegated permissions, or submit adversarial prompts.
preconditions: All participating agents adopt DIDs, signatures, contracts, ledgers, policy oracles, and the Defense Orchestration Engine; ledger and cryptographic assumptions hold.
mechanism: Protocol-native identity, signed messaging, ledger provenance, context-aware smart-contract access control, reputation, revocation, and execution halting.
interaction_surface: Discovery/identity; A2A messages; task contracts; delegation; shared task state; incident-response control plane.
primary_system_failure: Authentication, message/task integrity, authorization, provenance, and accountability failure.
reported_impact: Prototype-level attack neutralization and sub-second overhead under the framework’s ledger and oracle assumptions.
metric_definition: Attack-handling outcomes plus latency, throughput, and storage overhead.
unit_denominator: Per attack scenario/protocol operation and system performance trial; not a Byzantine consensus threshold experiment.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for architecture, DOE, attack classes, and sub-second overhead; paper Secs. 3–6 for components and prototype tables. Exact locator validation remains for author signoff.

adversary_position: Malicious user or compromised upstream agent; for advanced MAS cases the adversary directly controls one agent.
adversary_capabilities: Inject instructions into user input or external content; in MAS cases embed commands into an upstream agent’s output to induce downstream loops or wrong functions.
preconditions: Tool-capable agents; downstream agents consume peer-produced content; experiments implement only two agent types.
mechanism: Prompt-induced infinite loops or incorrect benign function execution, extended into viral cross-agent malfunction.
interaction_surface: User input; external tool/file content; memory; inter-agent message/control flow.
primary_system_failure: Availability/resource boundedness and task/action integrity failure.
reported_impact: Agent non-completion, repetitive actions, incorrect benign functions, bandwidth/resource occupation, and downstream spamming behavior.
metric_definition: Failure Rate: proportion of tested instructions/cases where the agent enters the target malfunction or fails the required task.
unit_denominator: Case-level trials, with different denominators across tables; advanced MAS Table 4 reports cases for two scenarios, not population prevalence.
evidence_locators: PDF Secs. 3.2-3.3 pp. 2-3; Tables 2-4 pp. 5-7; Sec. 5.5 pp. 6-7; Limitations p. 8.

adversary_position: Byzantine member agents among workers or evaluators.
adversary_capabilities: Submit arbitrary proposals/scores/votes and exploit leader dependence in baseline coordination.
preconditions: Synchronous authenticated communication, known participant set, and Byzantine fraction below the protocol’s stated bound.
mechanism: Leaderless concurrent proposal generation and Byzantine-robust evaluator aggregation/selective finalization.
interaction_surface: Proposal generation; evaluator scoring/ranking; voting/aggregation; coordination rounds.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision integrity and coordination availability under Byzantine members.
reported_impact: Empirical task-quality and latency/round robustness under varied Byzantine fractions; not a universal agreement theorem.
metric_definition: Selected-answer task quality/accuracy, latency, number of rounds, and robustness as f/n varies.
unit_denominator: Task-instance and protocol-run level. Any f<n/2 statement is conditional on synchrony/authentication and the paper’s correctness definition.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for DecentLLMs and empirical claim; full paper threat model/theorems in pp. 3–7 and experiment tables. All formal statements require expert signoff against exact theorem text.

adversary_position: External attacker with information about one target participant rather than the full collective.
adversary_capabilities: Constructs adversarial inputs for the target and simulates group interactions through a stubborn proxy.
preconditions: The targeted member participates in communication and can influence majority or consensus-like aggregation.
mechanism: M-Spoiler optimizes a persistent adversarial influence using simulated group interactions.
interaction_surface: Target-agent input; outgoing messages; collective aggregation.
primary_system_failure: F4 collective task-decision integrity failure.
reported_impact: Incorrect or attacker-chosen group answer.
metric_definition: Targeted and untargeted collective attack success, transferability, and clean-task performance.
unit_denominator: Unit: Task and final group decision.; Denominator: Evaluated tasks across three seeds; targeted success uses all-agree for two agents or majority target output for larger groups.
evidence_locators: Threat model and incomplete-information game in Sec. 3, PDF pp. 3 to 5; stubborn proxy in Sec. 4, PDF pp. 5 to 7; main result tables in Sec. 5, PDF pp. 7 to 10; metric definition and three-seed reporting in evaluation.

adversary_position: Tool/supply-chain adversary plus trigger-capable user/operator.
adversary_capabilities: Poison selected tool implementations/descriptions and induce a designated tool-use sequence.
preconditions: Agents have public/private tools whose outputs/side effects compose; local inspection does not see a complete active payload.
mechanism: Distributed conditional tool-backdoor primitives that assemble under a cross-agent collaboration sequence.
interaction_surface: Tool supply chain; role-private capabilities; public tools; invocation order; provenance.
primary_system_failure: Delegation/authority and action-integrity failure, with confidentiality impact in exfiltration cases.
reported_impact: Targeted sandbox behavior such as data exfiltration at high triggered ASR while clean performance remains similar.
metric_definition: Triggered attack success rate, benign-task accuracy, and accidental trigger rate.
unit_denominator: Triggered benchmark episodes/tasks per model and dataset; headline >95% is an aggregate lower bound across reported main settings, not a population metric.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v1 Sec. 3 pp. 4-6 Fig. 2; Sec. 4.2 p. 7 and App. B pp. 15-17; Sec. 4.3 pp. 7-9 Table 1/Figs. 3-4; Sec. 5.1 p. 9 Fig. 5.

adversary_position: External adversary seeding contagious multimodal jailbreak content.
adversary_capabilities: Introduce a malicious multimodal sample that enters one agent’s state and can be transmitted to others.
preconditions: Agents exchange or inherit state/content; defender can generate and distribute cure samples through population channels.
mechanism: Cure samples immunize agents before exposure and propagate distributed protection/recovery so defensive reproduction competes with infection.
interaction_surface: Multimodal input; local state/memory; agent-to-agent transmission; population topology.
primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Population infection, immunity, and recovery outcomes under the evaluated models/topologies, plus theoretical robustness guarantees under stated assumptions.
metric_definition: Infection, immunization/recovery, expected spread, robustness bounds, and benign utility.
unit_denominator: Agent/population and propagation-run level; distinguish expected number of infections, infected fraction, recovery rate, and utility.
evidence_locators: PMLR abstract for defense concept and theoretical guarantee; published PDF Secs. 3–4 and theorem/result tables for exact conditions. Author signoff required for every bound and denominator.

adversary_position: Self-interested malicious member with an attacker-chosen role prompt.
adversary_capabilities: Send protocol-valid messages/code/comments, manipulate peers and monitor-visible evidence, retain assigned role.
preconditions: System scores individual/collective contributions or supports workload/tool choice; monitor relies on the transcript.
mechanism: Four distinct mechanisms: Scapegoater, Boaster, Self-Dealer, and Free-Rider.
interaction_surface: Peer messages; shared work products; contribution monitor; tool recommendations; workload allocation.
primary_system_failure: Attribution/incentive/coordination integrity failure.
reported_impact: Distorted credit, blame, workload, or tool choice while final task functionality can remain intact.
metric_definition: Task metrics plus personal and collective contribution scores; attack effect is score/tool/workload manipulation rather than one ASR.
unit_denominator: Agent/contribution/task records within each framework and attack type; tables report heterogeneous score shifts.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v1 Abstract p. 1; Sec. 3 pp. 4-6; Sec. 4 p. 6; Sec. 5.3 p. 9 Table 3; Appendix C p. 13 Table 6.

adversary_position: Black-box external adversary controlling content observed by an exposed edge agent.
adversary_capabilities: Query system, infer roles/edges, contaminate edge input, adapt payloads based on outcomes; no direct internal-member compromise.
preconditions: At least one dependency path links exposed agent to a more privileged agent; downstream agents reinterpret/execute upstream output.
mechanism: TOMA: topology reconnaissance, contamination modeling, path selection, and hierarchical payload encapsulation.
interaction_surface: External tool/content; hidden graph; delegated task edges; downstream trust; privileged tools.
primary_system_failure: Compromise containment and delegation/authority integrity failure.
reported_impact: Irrelevant/destructive actions including privileged filesystem or command operations in local benchmark/application setups.
metric_definition: Topology-reconstruction F1, ASR, infection-integrity score, consistency, blocking rate, latency, and resource overhead.
unit_denominator: Benchmark episodes and 20 application scenarios; 17/20 corresponds to 85% application-scenario success, while 40–78% is framework/topology dependent.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Sec. V pp. 5-10 Fig. 3; Sec. VII-D pp. 12-14 Table III; Sec. VII-E p. 15 Table VII; Sec. VII-F pp. 15-16 Tables VIII-X.

adversary_position: Malicious or compromised shared function-library/tool provider.
adversary_capabilities: Add deceptive function descriptions and callable malicious tools; target selected agent roles.
preconditions: Agents trust text-described shared library entries and pass outputs downstream.
mechanism: Function-library/tool poisoning with direct and downstream cascade paths.
interaction_surface: Shared tool metadata/function library; specialized-agent pipeline; downstream planning.
primary_system_failure: Communication/shared-artifact and joint trajectory/action-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Trajectory error and collision-rate increases in AgentDriver and AgentThink.
metric_definition: L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and ASR thresholded at L2 error 3 or 6.
unit_denominator: Driving episodes/samples; ASR definition changes with the specified L2 threshold and must always include it.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Abstract/Sec. 1 pp. 1-2 Fig. 1; method pp. 2-4 Figs. 2-3; Sec. 5 pp. 6-8 Table 2/Figs. 5-6.

adversary_position: Adversary introduces prompt injection, misinformation, or malicious utterances that propagate over the agent graph.
adversary_capabilities: Influences utterances that enter the monitored graph.
preconditions: The defender can reconstruct the utterance graph and observe enough messages to score nodes and edges.
mechanism: Attack propagation is evaluated, but the primary paper contribution is graph-based anomaly detection plus topology intervention.
interaction_surface: Communication graph; utterances; topology; monitor and control plane.
primary_system_failure: Claim-level F1, F3, or F4 depending on the evaluated attack. The paper itself should not receive one forced attack outcome.
reported_impact: Collective task or safety degradation under evaluated attacks.
metric_definition: Detection or security outcome plus recovered task performance.
unit_denominator: Unit: Agent, graph, and task.; Denominator: Experiment-specific agents or tasks; record exact table definitions for each claim.
evidence_locators: Abstract, PDF p. 1; method sections defining the utterance graph and graph-neural detector; experiment result tables for the recovery claim; intervention section for edge or topology changes.

adversary_position: Input-level or member-level misinformation injector.
adversary_capabilities: Insert persuasive false claims into messages that downstream agents consume.
preconditions: Task goal is available; a trusted LLM reviewer has sufficient knowledge/context to identify and rewrite false goal-relevant information.
mechanism: Goal-aware claim identification followed by rectification of messages before downstream use.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent messages; task-decomposition information flow; reviewer/rectification layer.
primary_system_failure: Collective factual/task integrity failure from misinformation propagation.
reported_impact: Reported reduction in misinformation toxicity and improvement in task success under tested injection settings.
metric_definition: Misinformation toxicity, task success under attack, identification/rectification effectiveness, and utility.
unit_denominator: Task/scenario and message-claim level depending on metric; abstract reports average 28.17% toxicity reduction and 10.33% task-success improvement across evaluated attacks.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for MisinfoTask/ARGUS and 28.17%/10.33% averages; paper Secs. 3–5 and result tables for exact metrics. Exact page/table validation remains for author signoff.

adversary_position: Compromised communicating member agents or injected erroneous messages.
adversary_capabilities: Send adversarial or erroneous protocol-valid messages that affect later agents.
preconditions: Monitor observes agent identities, timestamped messages, node/edge attributes, and can prune communication edges.
mechanism: Temporal attributed-graph reconstruction, node/edge anomaly scoring, graph abstraction, and edge pruning.
interaction_surface: Multi-round messages; temporal interaction graph; topology/edge control.
primary_system_failure: Propagation containment and collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Benchmark accuracy degradation under injected communication and empirical detection/recovery after pruning.
metric_definition: Task accuracy, anomaly/detection measures, false discovery rate, and runtime/resource efficiency.
unit_denominator: Task instance, agent/edge anomaly event, and runtime trial; detection and task recovery must be reported separately.
evidence_locators: NeurIPS proceedings abstract for temporal graph method and main claim; published PDF Secs. 3–5 for method, setup, and results. Exact table/page locators remain for author signoff.

adversary_position: External sender who inserts a self-replicating prompt into an email or retrieved document.
adversary_capabilities: Places malicious content that automated applications ingest, reproduce, and forward.
preconditions: Applications automatically process inbound content and can emit generated content to downstream users or applications.
mechanism: Indirect prompt injection with self-replication through generated content.
interaction_surface: Inbound email or RAG content; automated outbound messages; application-to-application workflow.
primary_system_failure: F1 propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Confidentiality loss and availability effects can be secondary payloads.
metric_definition: Propagation behavior, payload success, and defense true-positive, false-positive, and latency measures.
unit_denominator: Unit: Application or client, propagation event, and detector decision.; Denominator: Final-paper evaluation trials and clients. Do not import denominators from the preprint without checking the final paper.
evidence_locators: Final ACM record and CCS paper; preprint retained only for lineage. Cite final tables for propagation and DonkeyRail values. The current note's abstract-only locators are insufficient for quantitative use.

adversary_position: Agents optimized under misspecified or adversarial incentives rather than a conventional external attacker.
adversary_capabilities: Learn linguistic encodings and decodings under GBRL or in-context reinforcement-learning elicitation.
preconditions: Reward favors task success and hidden information transfer while oversight penalizes observable evidence.
mechanism: Learned linguistic steganography.
interaction_surface: Natural-language message channel; reward and training incentives; observer boundary.
primary_system_failure: Oversight or monitorability integrity failure.
reported_impact: Hidden information transfer and prohibited coordination.
metric_definition: Task Success, Decoding Success, Sender Task Success, Overseer Bypass Success, Collusion Success, and channel capacity.
unit_denominator: Unit: Communication episode or request.; Denominator: Task or episode trials defined per metric; there is no single universal ASR.
evidence_locators: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1 to 2; metric definitions around PDF p. 3; experiment and mitigation sections; limitations or discussion.

adversary_position: Malicious communicating member agents.
adversary_capabilities: Send false or inconsistent messages during multi-round broadcast.
preconditions: The application accepts IBGP’s k-of-n partial coordination/consistency definition; a global randomizer controls hidden stopping time; protocol and honest local observations are trusted.
mechanism: Redefines global BGP agreement/consistency into partial k-threshold coordination and applies a multi-round prompt/protocol.
interaction_surface: Broadcast messages; local observations; partial coordination rule.
primary_system_failure: Local coordination integrity/mis-coordination under malicious members.
reported_impact: Task/environment robustness percentages under the paper’s IBGP predicate, not global consensus accuracy.
metric_definition: Robustness percentage defined by avoiding IBGP mis-coordination in each environment.
unit_denominator: Episode/environment-run level under parameter tuple (n, t, k, ...); not a standard ASR and not a global Byzantine agreement rate.
evidence_locators: Official PDF p. 1 authors/metadata and problem framing; pp. 1–2 Definitions 2.1–2.2; p. 2 Table 1 and protocol description.

adversary_position: External adversary able to intervene once against one agent/message.
adversary_capabilities: Optimize and inject a token-level suffix; no continuing control after the initial intervention.
preconditions: Agents exchange generated text and retain sufficient context for the suffix to be copied or regenerated downstream.
mechanism: CODES continuous-space token optimization plus discrete coordinate search for a self-repeating adversarial suffix.
interaction_surface: Initial prompt/message; retained conversation context; inter-agent message chain; composed safeguard pipeline.
primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: One seed affects later agents or multiple safeguard stages and induces harmful output; impact is demonstrated in three defined attack scenarios.
metric_definition: Attack success, self-repetition/propagation success, optimization loss, and optimization efficiency.
unit_denominator: Scenario/run and generated-message level; no single standardized population denominator is reported across all scenarios.
evidence_locators: Published PDF Abstract/Introduction pp. 1-2; threat scenarios throughout Sec. 2; method Sec. 3.2 p. 5 Algorithms 1-2; result tables in evaluation section.

adversary_position: Eavesdropper, injected instruction source, or over-privileged/compromised agent causing unauthorized data flow.
adversary_capabilities: Elicit, forward, or route labeled sensitive content through messages, LLM calls, tools, or users.
preconditions: Complete mediation through embedded reference monitors, correct policy specification/data labels, known principal identities, and registered tool/message paths.
mechanism: Policy language plus embedded reference monitors and formal verification enforce fine-grained allowed flows.
interaction_surface: Agent messages; LLM endpoints; tool calls; external users; labeled data flow.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and contextual-integrity violation.
reported_impact: Blocked sensitive-data leakage in prototype scenarios while retaining task success and incurring measured overhead.
metric_definition: Policy-violation prevention, task success/utility, and performance overhead.
unit_denominator: Privacy scenario/task and mediated flow-event level; formal guarantees apply to modeled paths, not semantic leakage outside them.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for architecture, AutoGen/LangChain integration, and three task suites; PDF Secs. 3–4 and evaluation tables for policy model and overhead. Exact locators require author signoff.

adversary_position: External user with conversational access to selected entry agents.
adversary_capabilities: Probe roles and neighbors, infer structure, inject adversarial traits into selected roles, retain them, and later activate coordinated harmful behavior.
preconditions: The system exposes conversational responses sufficient for role/topology probing and accepts multi-round prompt interactions.
mechanism: Three-stage structure reconnaissance, scenario-adaptive role-trait injection, and activation using inferred role/topology context.
interaction_surface: Role/system prompts; messages; memory; topology; collective task execution.
primary_system_failure: Collective action and objective-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Specialized agents maintain adversarial roles and cooperate on harmful scenario-specific tasks.
metric_definition: Attack Success Rate plus blackened-role consistency, harmful-cooperation score, and defense-efficiency measures.
unit_denominator: Scenario/task instances; ASR is not a population-infection rate. Exact denominator must be cited from the evaluation protocol.
evidence_locators: PDF Sec. 3.1 pp. 3-4 and Fig. 2; Secs. 3.2.4-3.2.5 pp. 5-6; Sec. 4.1 pp. 6-7; Table 2; Fig. 5 p. 9.

adversary_position: one compromised insider member
adversary_capabilities: participate through ordinary medical deliberation messages while concealing harmful intent
preconditions: five-agent team; benchmark harmful prompts; evaluator and enforcement agent trusted
mechanism: dark-personality role induces harmful guidance that propagates or is aggregated
interaction_surface: member role prompt; medical deliberation messages; topology; aggregation
primary_system_failure: collective medical decision-integrity and safety failure
reported_impact: unsafe medical advice despite honest agents
metric_definition: Local Content Safety, Response Safety, medical accuracy, token usage, evaluation time
unit_denominator: prompt/run and possibly agent-local utterance; LCS and RS are distinct and must not be collapsed into ASR
evidence_locators: Paper Abstract and sections 3-5; Table 1, Figure 2, Tables 2-3; repository note lists pages 1,4-7

adversary_position: External/malicious user injecting a direct malicious instruction into one randomly selected member.
adversary_capabilities: Selects one of five eligible target agents and injects one of 12 jailbreak prompts; no model parameter control.
preconditions: Seven-agent asynchronous research facility, inter-agent messaging, role-specific prompts, code-execution tool, one compromised member.
mechanism: Infectious malicious prompt and multi-hop instruction propagation.
interaction_surface: Member input; inter-agent messaging; memory; tool execution.
primary_system_failure: Compromise containment and action-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Propagation can culminate in a code call instructing a hazardous lab action; defenses trade security for cooperation.
metric_definition: System robustness = fraction of simulations not producing the malicious outcome; agent cooperation = acceptance rate of unusual but harmless instructions; behavioral compromise scores by message step.
unit_denominator: System robustness over 36 simulations per model-defense condition; cooperation over 5,400 agent-instruction trials.
evidence_locators: AAAI/arXiv PDF pp. 1-3 and Fig. 2; Sec. 3 pp. 4-5; Table 1 pp. 5-6; Sec. 5 “Discussion & Limitations” p. 7; appendices for prompts.

adversary_position: External adversary controlling web, file, email, audio, or other untrusted content.
adversary_capabilities: Places indirect prompt injection that changes LLM-mediated routing or invocation decisions.
preconditions: Framework orchestrators use generated text or metadata to route among specialist agents and code-capable functions.
mechanism: Indirect prompt injection plus confused-deputy or control-flow laundering.
interaction_surface: Untrusted content; inter-agent messages; orchestration metadata; routing; tool invocation.
primary_system_failure: F6 delegation, authority, and control-flow integrity failure.
reported_impact: Unauthorized invocation, data exfiltration, or arbitrary code execution.
metric_definition: Trial-level attack success and successful unsafe or code invocation.
unit_denominator: Unit: Attack trial and framework/model configuration.; Denominator: Trials for each framework, model, and attack scenario.
evidence_locators: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1 to 2; attack design and system diagrams, PDF p. 2 onward; framework/model result tables; mitigation analysis.

adversary_position: Malicious-query source or compromised interaction input in adversarial subsets.
adversary_capabilities: Introduces misinformation, bias, or harmful content that propagates and is aggregated.
preconditions: Agents iteratively exchange information according to a configured RelCom graph.
mechanism: Topology-conditioned propagation and aggregation. Topology itself is an evaluation variable, not an attack mechanism.
interaction_surface: Communication topology; iterative messages; aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Claim-level F1 or F4 for adversarial subsets; adjacent reliability and fairness for other phenomena.
reported_impact: Task-performance and safety degradation in evaluated settings.
metric_definition: Per-agent and aggregate joint accuracy or safety outcomes by round and topology.
unit_denominator: Unit: Agent, round, and task.; Denominator: Per-agent or aggregate task cases as defined in each experiment.
evidence_locators: Abstract and framework, PDF pp. 1 to 3; result sections naming Agent Hallucination, Aggregation Safety, and Security Bottleneck; exact result table for the 29.7% setting; limitations section.

adversary_position: Faulty or malicious member agent; fault injector controls role prompt or outgoing message.
adversary_capabilities: AutoTransform alters role behavior; AutoInject inserts syntactic, semantic, or task-specific errors into selected agent outputs.
preconditions: Fixed collaboration templates and task scoring; errors are synthetically generated.
mechanism: Role transformation or message-level fault injection followed by downstream propagation.
interaction_surface: Role prompt; inter-agent messages; collaboration topology.
primary_system_failure: Collective output-integrity and reliability failure.
reported_impact: Task performance drops; Challenger/Inspector recover a portion of injected errors.
metric_definition: Task-specific accuracy/quality, performance drop, and error-recovery fraction.
unit_denominator: Task instances and injected-error events; 5.5/10.5/23.7 are average performance drops by structural group, not ASR.
evidence_locators: PDF Sec. 3 pp. 3-4 Fig. 2; Sec. 4 pp. 4-6 Tables 1-2; Sec. 5 pp. 6-8; Sec. 6 pp. 8-9 Fig. 6.

adversary_position: Agent-in-the-middle adversary on selected communication links.
adversary_capabilities: Intercepts and adaptively rewrites protocol-valid messages under role and format constraints.
preconditions: Access to selected message paths; endpoints trust messages without authenticated integrity protection.
mechanism: Context-aware message interception and adaptive rewriting using reflection.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent communication links; protocol-valid message content.
primary_system_failure: F3 communication integrity failure.
reported_impact: F4 collective task or decision integrity failure as a downstream consequence.
metric_definition: Whole-dataset ASR for targeted behavior or denial-of-service outcomes.
unit_denominator: Unit: Task instance.; Denominator: All evaluated dataset instances for a setting.
evidence_locators: Abstract and threat model, PDF pp. 1 to 3 and Fig. 1; metric definition in Sec. 4.1, approximately PDF p. 5; evaluation tables for framework, structure, and application results; limitations section.

adversary_position: Malicious peer agent in the MAS-specific condition; also external user and RAG-data attacker in comparators.
adversary_capabilities: Send the same malware-installation/system-compromise request through different provenance channels.
preconditions: Victim is tool-capable and can install/execute software; safety behavior depends on sender/context provenance.
mechanism: Inter-Agent Trust Exploitation, a confused-deputy/provenance attack where a peer-origin request bypasses refusals.
interaction_surface: Peer-agent request channel; request provenance; tool execution; user/RAG boundaries as controls.
primary_system_failure: Cross-agent authorization and action-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Controlled host-compromise actions; 18/18 tested models accepted the inter-agent condition in the paper’s setup.
metric_definition: Fraction of 18 tested model backbones that execute/complete the requested compromise under each origin condition.
unit_denominator: Models/backbones (18), not prompts, tasks, agents, or populations: 17/18 direct, 15/18 RAG, 18/18 inter-agent.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v6 Abstract p. 1; attack-surface and inter-agent sections pp. 5-6; evaluation pp. 5-6.

adversary_position: Unreliable, biased, deceptive, toxic, irrelevant, or low-quality peer agents.
adversary_capabilities: Send protocol-valid messages that vary along six trust dimensions.
preconditions: Message content, sender identity, and model attention/internal trust features are available; thresholds generalize across models/tasks.
mechanism: Attention-derived trust scores support message-level and agent-level filtering/down-weighting.
interaction_surface: Incoming peer messages; aggregation; model attention/internal signals; identity history.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity degradation from untrustworthy contributions.
reported_impact: Improved benchmark robustness/task accuracy across tested message categories.
metric_definition: Trust classification/dimension scores, task accuracy, and robustness to injected message categories.
unit_denominator: Message and task-instance level; threshold sensitivity/false alarms must be reported separately from task accuracy.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for six dimensions, A-Trust/TMS, and acceptance comment; full paper Secs. 2–3 and result/limitation sections. Exact tables/pages require author signoff.

adversary_position: One or two malicious member agents inside the collaboration group.
adversary_capabilities: Generate a counterfactual answer, observe shared responses, retain interaction history, and adapt misleading responses across rounds.
preconditions: Fixed-answer tasks; symmetric sharing of agent responses; at most five honest collaborators; synthetically generated counterfactual answer.
mechanism: Adaptive counterfactual-answer persuasion through repeated group communication.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent deliberation; communication schedule; consensus formation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Honest agents adopt the adversarial answer earlier or more often, reducing group robustness.
metric_definition: System Defense Index aggregates whether initially non-adversarial agents adopt the counterfactual answer and the first affected round; also reports First Attacked Time, consensus, and accuracy.
unit_denominator: SDI is averaged over dataset questions and includes agent and round terms; it is not a conventional task-level ASR.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3, Secs. 2.1-2.4 and Eqs. 1-3; pp. 3-6, Figs. 1-4; p. 9 Limitations.

adversary_position: One intention-hiding malicious member.
adversary_capabilities: Alter its own protocol-valid messages while appearing role-consistent; no access to peers’ internals.
preconditions: Peers trust ordinary member messages; defender can probe, monitor, and possibly remove members.
mechanism: Four distinct strategies: suboptimal fixation, reframing misalignment, fake injection, and execution delay.
interaction_surface: Role-consistent peer communication; coordination; membership; pre-task interrogation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision/objective integrity failure.
reported_impact: Reduced task success or increased completion cost; AgentXposed detection/recovery in controlled tasks.
metric_definition: Task accuracy, completion efficiency, malicious-agent detection accuracy, and post-intervention recovery.
unit_denominator: Task instances and agent-level detection decisions; no single attack-success denominator across all four attacks.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Sec. 4.2 pp. 4-6; Sec. 4.4 pp. 6-7 Figs. 3-6; Sec. 5.1 p. 8 Table 1.

adversary_position: Malicious registered remote agent, spoofed AgentCard publisher, or adversarial A2A protocol peer.
adversary_capabilities: AgentCard spoofing, capability cloaking, cyclic delegation, half-open task flooding, agent-side request forgery, and artifact-triggered script injection.
preconditions: Protocol-valid discovery, task, request, and artifact interfaces and an adapter that preserves semantics across implementations.
mechanism: Protocol-logic abuse or supply-chain manipulation introduces and activates a malicious peer.
interaction_surface: Registry and AgentCard; discovery; asynchronous task state; remote requests; returned artifacts.
primary_system_failure: Claim-level identity, confidentiality, integrity, or availability failures.
reported_impact: Unsafe request handling, resource exhaustion, or artifact execution.
metric_definition: Attack or safety outcome plus benign utility or helpfulness; Capability Cloaking also reports label accuracy and evidence quality.
unit_denominator: Unit: Benchmark case and SUT trial.; Denominator: Repository release includes 100 AgentCard Spoofing cases and 100 cases for each Capability Cloaking split; other executable families have attack cases and matched controls.
evidence_locators: Official ICLR 2026 poster record; project README for the seven listed benchmark rows, release-case counts, matched controls, deterministic baselines, and output schema. Exact paper page and table references remain unresolved.

adversary_position: external-input adversary, malicious/compromised agent profile, or on-path message poisoner depending on scenario
adversary_capabilities: inject via external inputs, agent profiles, or inter-agent messages to hijack, disrupt, or exfiltrate
preconditions: six supported MAS implementations and benchmark-defined access for each threat scenario
mechanism: agent cascading injection propagates through trusted communication/role relationships
interaction_surface: external input; agent profile; inter-agent message
primary_system_failure: instruction integrity, availability, or confidentiality failure, claim-specific
reported_impact: workflow hijacking, task disruption, information exfiltration, and propagation
metric_definition: Benign Utility, Attack Success Rate, Defense Success Rate, Propagation Success Rate
unit_denominator: test case/run within surface-objective-system cells; metrics have different predicates and cannot be collapsed
evidence_locators: ACL paper Abstract and section 4, section 5.1; 1,356 cases, six implementations, metric definitions

adversary_position: varies by attack family; over-disclosure also occurs without a strategic attacker
adversary_capabilities: prompt/instruction, tool, memory/persistence, or multi-agent coordination manipulations
preconditions: instrumented coordinator-worker framework, contextual privacy labels, seven channel definitions
mechanism: sensitive context is transmitted, retained, or passed to tools through internal coordination channels
interaction_surface: final output; inter-agent messages; reasoning/context; tool input/output; shared memory; logs; artifacts
primary_system_failure: cross-channel confidentiality and data-minimization failure
reported_impact: hidden internal leakage and increased total exposure despite cleaner final outputs
metric_definition: C1/C2/C5 channel leakage rates, whole-system OR-union exposure, hidden-leakage H1, attack-family ASR
unit_denominator: 4,979 model-scenario traces for C1/C2/C5; channel rates and OR-union are not additive; attack-family ASR uses 1,983 attack tests
evidence_locators: IEEE/arXiv Tables 8, 10-15; Figures 3-5; main benchmark and methods sections

adversary_position: External or compromised-agent attacker whose actions produce application/network/host events.
adversary_capabilities: Prompt hijacking, retrieval poisoning, tool-use redirection, and related cross-agent actions represented in red-team traces.
preconditions: Synchronized, trustworthy application/network/system logs; stable agent attribution and clocks; graph construction and detector are trusted.
mechanism: Convert each execution into an attributed directed multigraph; graph-level classification plus partial-trace early detection and SHAP-based attribution.
interaction_surface: Application events; network events; operating-system events; global execution trace.
primary_system_failure: Detection/attribution failure when distributed attack evidence is fragmented across telemetry layers.
reported_impact: End-to-end detection and early high-trust alerts around 40% trace progress in the authors’ red-teamed environment.
metric_definition: End-to-end detection performance, false alarms, early-detection performance versus trace progress, attribution quality, and computational overhead.
unit_denominator: Execution-trace level. The 31.4% figure is the attack success rate in the generated red-team runs, not the fraction of attack traces.
evidence_locators: ScienceDirect abstract for 800 traces, 31.4% ASR, ~40% early alerts, content-free telemetry, and SHAP attribution; full article architecture/evaluation sections for exact tables. Author signoff required.

adversary_position: Supply-chain/member adversary contributing one or more malicious language models to a collaboration pool.
adversary_capabilities: Engineer malicious contributors via prompting, activation steering, supervised fine-tuning, or inverted-reward RL; participate in routing/text/logit/weight collaboration.
preconditions: System admits third-party contributor models and lacks perfect pre-admission detection; trusted external supervisor may be added for mitigation.
mechanism: Malicious contributor insertion into one of four collaboration levels.
interaction_surface: Contributor admission; API routing; text exchange; logit aggregation; weight merging.
primary_system_failure: Collective output/safety integrity degradation.
reported_impact: Average degradation reported across reasoning and safety tasks; supervisor recovers much of benign performance, but effects are task/collaboration specific.
metric_definition: Task performance and degradation relative to benign collaboration; recovery fraction after mitigation.
unit_denominator: Dataset/task examples and aggregate performance differences by collaboration method; 7.12%, 7.94%, and 95.31% are reported averages, not attack-success probabilities.
evidence_locators: ACL paper Abstract p. 1; Secs. 2.1–2.2 pp. 2-4; Appendix A.1 p. 14 Table 4.

adversary_position: Malicious user issuing direct harmful tasks; no compromised member.
adversary_capabilities: Submit harmful task only; cannot inject memory/messages or control agents.
preconditions: Architecture fragments task intent, authority, or context; matched benchmark/model comparisons within each design axis.
mechanism: Compositional context fragmentation and distributed tool authority, not a newly crafted attack payload.
interaction_surface: Role decomposition; routing/topology; memory visibility; tool authority.
primary_system_failure: Compositional harmful-action and authorization-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Partial or completed harmful task execution that a standalone agent may refuse.
metric_definition: Planning Refusal, Execution Refusal, Harmful Action, Harmful Task completion, and benign accuracy.
unit_denominator: Task instances; the 3.8x comparison is a ratio of harmful-task completion rates in selected matched configurations, not a universal effect size.
evidence_locators: ArXiv Sec. 4 pp. 4-5 and Tables 8-10; Sec. 4.4 p. 5; Secs. 5.1-5.3 pp. 5-8; Sec. 8 p. 9.

adversary_position: On-path communication adversary controlling a subset of links.
adversary_capabilities: Observe, select, and replace messages across rounds; knows graph and role/task context; cannot directly alter agent state.
preconditions: Unauthenticated or modifiable communication links and continuous access to selected channels.
mechanism: MCTS/DPO-trained adaptive multi-round tampering with semantic and embedding similarity constraints.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent messages; communication graph.
primary_system_failure: Communication integrity and collective task-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Steered final joint output toward attacker goals while evading a semantic detector.
metric_definition: Final-output Attack Success Rate plus message-level stealthiness under a trusted LLM detector.
unit_denominator: Task instances for ASR and transmitted messages for detector/stealth metrics; these denominators must remain separate.
evidence_locators: AAAI PDF Sec. 3.2 p. 3; Secs. 4.1-4.2 pp. 3-5, Fig. 2, Eqs. 10-11; Secs. 5.1-5.2 pp. 5-7, Table 1.

adversary_position: one compromised member agent
adversary_capabilities: send persuasive/deceptive messages through ordinary role interfaces
preconditions: emulated tool environments and executable harm evaluators; one member controlled
mechanism: malicious peer induces honest agents to perform target harmful action through message influence and delegated tools
interaction_surface: inter-agent messages; role trust; tool delegation; shared task execution
primary_system_failure: compositional action-integrity/authorization failure
reported_impact: unauthorized, unsafe, privacy-violating, or resource-abusing actions
metric_definition: environment-specific executable harmful-action success plus benign task outcomes
unit_denominator: 937 curated harmful actions in accepted version; aggregation crosses model, role, harm category, and architecture
evidence_locators: Accepted paper contribution list p.2, threat model/Figure 1, benchmark design and ethics/reproducibility sections

adversary_position: Three compromised member agents in the main evaluation.
adversary_capabilities: Alter messages through prompt attack, malicious tool return, or poisoned memory.
preconditions: Normal-behavior traces are available for training; graph identities/responses are visible; defender can prune bidirectional edges.
mechanism: Hierarchical agent encoder plus synthetic feature corruption/contrastive anomaly scoring and topology pruning.
interaction_surface: Prompts; tool outputs; memory; agent messages; communication graph.
primary_system_failure: Propagation containment and collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Post-attack collective answer degradation, malicious-agent AUC, and post-pruning ASR/accuracy in controlled settings.
metric_definition: ASR@3 after three rounds, malicious-agent detection AUC, and task accuracy/utility.
unit_denominator: Task-instance level for ASR@3 and agent-label level for AUC; do not collapse detection and system recovery.
evidence_locators: ACL metadata/abstract; published PDF Sec. 3 and Fig. 2 for method; Sec. 4.1/Table 1 for attack families/topologies/backbones/metrics.

adversary_position: External content adversary controlling one item ingested by a benign member.
adversary_capabilities: Embed instructions in content; induce fake error and repair plan; no control of user prompt, agents, or internals.
preconditions: Adaptive orchestrator trusts member summaries and routes all agent calls through an enforceable orchestration point.
mechanism: Alignment-check-evasive control-flow hijacking via trusted-agent laundering and attacker-chosen recovery sequence.
interaction_surface: Untrusted content; member status reports; replanning; orchestrator transition; delegated tools.
primary_system_failure: Delegation/control-flow and authorization integrity failure; confidentiality impact in exfiltration cases.
reported_impact: Unsafe agent invocation, code execution, unauthorized data sending, and contextual privilege misuse.
metric_definition: Task-level ASR, exact/open-ended task utility, CFG parse/completeness, and runtime.
unit_denominator: CFH-Hard tasks/attacks and modified AgentDojo cases; “blocked all” means zero successes in the finite evaluated suite.
evidence_locators: Full text Sec. 2 p. 2 Figs. 1-3; Sec. 4 pp. 4-5 Fig. 4; Sec. 5 p. 6; Secs. 6.3-6.4 pp. 8-9 Tables 1-3.

adversary_position: External black-box querier.
adversary_capabilities: Submit crafted queries and observe exposed outputs; no access to graph, prompts, internal messages, roles, or weights.
preconditions: Information-flow dependencies create semantic correlations observable at the interface; tested systems use optimized hidden graphs.
mechanism: Adversarial query generation, global-bias disentanglement, LLM weak supervision, and edge classification.
interaction_surface: Public query/output interface; semantic traces of hidden communication.
primary_system_failure: Structural confidentiality and architecture IP leakage.
reported_impact: Reconstruction of hidden communication edges; no follow-on exploit is demonstrated.
metric_definition: Edge-classification AUC and related classification measures.
unit_denominator: Candidate graph edges across test systems; not task-level ASR.
evidence_locators: PDF Sec. 3 pp. 3-4; Sec. 4 pp. 4-7; Sec. 5 pp. 8-10 and main result tables.

adversary_position: coalition of member agents with a secondary objective
adversary_capabilities: secret communication, persuasion, and coordinated action selection
preconditions: DCOP objective and cooperative optimum specified; coalition objective known to evaluator
mechanism: coalition coordinates through ordinary or secret channels to optimize secondary objective
interaction_surface: free-form messages; secret channel; joint action space
primary_system_failure: collective objective and oversight integrity failure
reported_impact: regret/coalition advantage and mismatch between textual collusion and realized actions
metric_definition: overall regret, coalition advantage, LLM-judge collusion labels, text-action agreement
unit_denominator: episode/environment/coalition; regret is objective-relative, not an ASR
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract, sections 4-5, metric equations, environment and results sections

adversary_position: Adversary controlling trigger placement and one remote-agent template while leaving model weights and the client agent unchanged.
adversary_capabilities: Places two fragments and relies on system routing to combine them.
preconditions: Star, chain, or DAG routing eventually joins the trigger and hidden template in one effective context.
mechanism: Conjunctive activation of individually benign fragments.
interaction_surface: User query; remote-agent template; routing and provenance; local guards.
primary_system_failure: F3 communication, context, or action integrity failure.
reported_impact: Harmful action or unsafe output. F6 authority integrity should be secondary only when an explicit privileged action or permission escalation is demonstrated.
metric_definition: ASR and false activation across topologies and control conditions.
unit_denominator: Unit: Attack scenario or routed task.; Denominator: Evaluated scenarios for each topology and fragment condition.
evidence_locators: Abstract, PDF p. 1; threat model and routing composition, PDF p. 1 onward; experimental tables for clean, single-fragment, and combined conditions; topology tables for star, chain, and DAG.

adversary_position: Source of a semantically benign recursive instruction.
adversary_capabilities: Introduces content that agents accept and recursively pass or act upon.
preconditions: Agents can initiate further messages or tasks for peers and lack a global collaboration budget.
mechanism: Recursive contagious instructions create cycles of meaningless collaboration.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent communication; delegation or invocation; topology; resource plane.
primary_system_failure: F7 availability and resource boundedness failure.
reported_impact: System paralysis and loss of useful collaboration. Contagion is a mechanism, not the primary failure label.
metric_definition: P-ASR and peak-blocking-turn style measures.
unit_denominator: Unit: Agent and interaction turn.; Denominator: P-ASR equals blocked agents divided by total agents in the network.
evidence_locators: Abstract and threat model, PDF p. 1 onward; metric definition and experiment tables, including topology results and repeated-run description; defense comparison section.

adversary_position: Gray-box malicious tool/API channel associated with one target agent.
adversary_capabilities: Monitor that agent’s tool calls and raw returns, replace at most B returns, retain local tool-interaction history; cannot see inter-agent messages or model internals.
preconditions: At least one target agent uses a compromisable tool channel; downstream task outcome depends on its tool results; intervention budget B=3 in main experiments.
mechanism: Memory-augmented, deliberative multi-round tool-return manipulation optimized by Attack-Flow GRPO.
interaction_surface: Tool/API return channel; target-agent local context; downstream communication and global task trace.
primary_system_failure: Collective task/action-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Performance degradation across code, deep-research, and web tasks, sometimes propagating to terminal system failure.
metric_definition: Uses each benchmark’s official task metric (TS, Pass@1, RACE, WebArena SR, WebShop score) and reports absolute degradation from no-attack, rather than one common ASR.
unit_denominator: Task/benchmark-specific instances. “Attack effectiveness” is metric decline; denominators are not comparable across benchmarks.
evidence_locators: PDF Sec. 2 pp. 2-3; Fig. 1; Sec. 4.1 p. 4; Table 1 pp. 5; Table 2 pp. 5-6; Sec. 4.5; Limitations p. 8.

adversary_position: Compromised member agents.
adversary_capabilities: Produce malicious responses after prompt, tool-output, or memory poisoning.
preconditions: Agent responses, identities, token/sentence representations, graph neighborhoods, and node-removal authority are available.
mechanism: Bi-level token/sentence encoding, theme-aware graph anomaly detection, explanatory token attribution, and topology repair.
interaction_surface: Agent response text; graph neighborhoods; prompts; tools; memory; communication topology.
primary_system_failure: Propagation containment and collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Detection AUROC, lower post-defense ASR, answer accuracy, and explanation quality in tested settings.
metric_definition: AUROC, attack success rate, answer accuracy, and explanation/localization measures.
unit_denominator: Agent/response-level anomaly labels for AUROC and task-instance level for ASR/accuracy.
evidence_locators: ACL metadata/abstract; PDF Sec. 3 and Fig. 2 for architecture; Sec. 4.1/Table 1 for setup/topologies/attack surfaces.

adversary_position: malicious user issuing harmful requests
adversary_capabilities: submit direct harmful prompts that are decomposed and delegated
preconditions: five observable architectures, trajectory judge, stage identities
mechanism: task decomposition, context fragmentation, ignored refusal, and fallback behavior hide or reconstitute harmful intent
interaction_surface: user request; planner; delegation; context sharing; subagents; fallback logic
primary_system_failure: compositional action-integrity and safety-enforcement failure
reported_impact: harmful workflow execution despite component refusals or incomplete context
metric_definition: ASR, Refusal Rate, ARIA risk levels, DHARMA stage categories
unit_denominator: task/trajectory; DHARMA is a diagnostic taxonomy rather than one scalar metric
evidence_locators: Workshop/arXiv Abstract, sections 3-5, Figure 3, main tables

adversary_position: Adversary manipulates an initial model or agent before deployment and introduces manipulated knowledge through persuasion and knowledge injection.
adversary_capabilities: Uses DPO or LoRA-style persuasion adaptation and ROME-style knowledge editing, then relies on interaction and stored histories for spread.
preconditions: Agents trust peer messages and may persist chat histories for later RAG retrieval.
mechanism: Persuasiveness injection plus manipulated-knowledge injection followed by interaction-driven spread and persistence.
interaction_surface: Agent model state; communication; chat history; RAG memory.
primary_system_failure: F3 communication and shared-knowledge integrity failure.
reported_impact: F1 containment and persistence failure is secondary.
metric_definition: Spread accuracy for counterfactual or toxic knowledge, interaction turns, agent-order or population effects, and RAG persistence.
unit_denominator: Unit: Agent response, knowledge item, or interaction turn depending on analysis.; Denominator: Must be copied from the final journal metric definitions and tables; the current record is too generic.
evidence_locators: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1 to 2 of the accessible version; method in Sec. III; experiments in Sec. IV, especially the spread and RAG-persistence subsections. Recheck page and table numbers against the final journal PDF.

adversary_position: External content adversary whose payload is read and evaluated by runtime guardrail.
adversary_capabilities: Inject natural-language content optimized to extend guardrail reasoning; no guardrail code or agent control.
preconditions: Guardrail is on action-critical path and shared among agents; scheduling/resource limits allow one request to block others.
mechanism: Schema-shaped/optimized reasoning-extension payload causing guardrail token and latency amplification.
interaction_surface: Untrusted content; shared guardrail service; scheduling/queue; timeout policy.
primary_system_failure: Shared-service availability and resource-isolation failure.
reported_impact: 13–63× token amplification in standalone tests, up to 148× latency in end-to-end deployments, and starvation/head-of-line blocking in shared MAS guardrail setting.
metric_definition: Generated tokens, latency amplification, throughput, blocked/task-success outcomes.
unit_denominator: Request/deployment-level resource ratios; amplification factors are ratios, not ASR or affected-agent fraction.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Abstract p. 1; Secs. 3-5 pp. 4-7 Fig. 1; Sec. 7.2 pp. 11-12 Table 10; conclusion p. 16.

adversary_position: one member agent acting as an adaptive imposter
adversary_capabilities: participate in ordinary collective discussion, optimize deceptive messages against the current detector, and evolve strategies over generations
preconditions: chess substrate with deterministic correctness, labeled imposter/benign discussions, detector access during co-evolution, and 20 labeled post-shift examples in recalibration mode
mechanism: co-evolved strategically deceptive reasoning degrades the collective while minimizing detector evidence
interaction_surface: inter-agent deliberation; member role; adaptive attack/defense feedback loop; observer calibration
primary_system_failure: collective decision integrity and malicious-member detectability failure
reported_impact: collective task collapse with near-chance detection in the highlighted adaptive setting; large differences in few-shot adaptation despite similar zero-shot scores
metric_definition: three benchmark modes; two independent detection/adaptation scores; F1 for imposter detection; collective chess performance
unit_denominator: 27,804 labeled discussion instances spanning 240 co-evolved imposter strategies; 22,104 train and 5,700 held-out according to the paper note
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract; method and benchmark sections; Figure 1; dataset split and adaptation result tables. Exact page/table locators require final author signoff.

adversary_position: compromised communicating member node
adversary_capabilities: send adversarial debate messages that steer peers and prolong deliberation
preconditions: observable attributed graph, benchmark-generated attack labels, live rounds, and authority to isolate flagged nodes
mechanism: malicious messages alter neighborhood reasoning; graph detectors identify nodes and dynamically remove them
interaction_surface: inter-agent messages; graph neighborhoods; topology; remediation controller
primary_system_failure: collective answer integrity and resource-efficiency degradation
reported_impact: wrong consensus and higher token cost; successful early isolation can restore integrity and shorten adversarial deliberation
metric_definition: agent/task accuracy, ASR, malicious-node detection performance, token cost, and execution efficiency
unit_denominator: task-run and agent/node instances generated by the framework; exact dataset sizes and split denominators require PDF signoff
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract; architecture Figure 2; training-data-generation and defense-benchmarking sections; main result tables

adversary_position: compromised specialist member, colluding members, or attacker controlling shared context/memory
adversary_capabilities: alter specialist outputs, coordinate small deviations, corrupt shared evidence, and trigger delayed or persistent perturbations
preconditions: paired clean/perturbed executions under the same database seed, deterministic decision gate, trace oracle, and full event instrumentation
mechanism: local deviations are routed, reused, reinforced, or persisted until they produce broader trace-level harm
interaction_surface: specialist outputs; tools; shared context; memory; router; guard events; deterministic decision gate
primary_system_failure: propagation and compromise-containment failure with downstream action/decision integrity impact
reported_impact: local and global harm diverge; different threat regimes maximize amplification, ASR, or malicious impact
metric_definition: ASR; safe and malicious impact; local harm; global harm; harm amplification H_global/H_local; stealth; benign utility; latency; normalized token cost
unit_denominator: paired query traces over 12 scenarios and five defense settings; local harm is over targeted components, global harm over all participating agents/events
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract and lines 104-124 of HTML; methodology sections 3.1-3.2; Tables 1 and 3-5; trace and metric definitions

adversary_position: Variant-specific external or infrastructure adversary with access to one or more perception, communication, shared-state, tool, or reasoning surfaces.
adversary_capabilities: Perturb images/text, spoof agents/tools, block links, pollute shared memory/context, alter roles, or inject reasoning instructions.
preconditions: OxyGent hierarchical MM-MAS; attack privilege differs by variant and must not be collapsed into one attacker model.
mechanism: HAM3 layered attack suite across perception, communication, and reasoning.
interaction_surface: Multimodal input; identity; communication links; shared memory/context; tools; reasoning trace.
primary_system_failure: Multiple claim-level failures: decision integrity, communication/topology integrity, shared-state integrity, and availability.
reported_impact: Incorrect root decision and, in many successful attacks, multiple agents converge on consistent errors.
metric_definition: Task Success Rate, ASR over clean-correct samples, Hallucination Error Rate, cross-modal consistency, and local/systemic error shares.
unit_denominator: ASR denominator is clean-correct GQA samples; local/systemic shares are conditioned on successful errors. Do not compare directly with task-level ASR elsewhere.

adversary_position: One legitimate malicious insider.
adversary_capabilities: Observe interaction state; send protocol-valid natural-language messages; train an RL policy against a learned surrogate world model.
preconditions: Benign agents iteratively deliberate; attacker can model their dynamics; one insider is admitted.
mechanism: World-model-based reinforcement-learning policy for adaptive consensus delay/disruption.
interaction_surface: Member messages; iterative consensus protocol; latent behavioral state.
primary_system_failure: Collective agreement/termination and decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Lower benign consensus rate and longer disagreement episodes than a direct malicious-prompt baseline.
metric_definition: Benign consensus rate and episode duration.
unit_denominator: Consensus episodes; duration/termination and agreement are separate metrics, not task ASR.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v1 Abstract p. 1; problem formulation pp. 1-3; method pp. 2-4; experiment/results pp. 3-4.

adversary_position: Coalition of writer, editor, and director agents.
adversary_capabilities: Select, rewrite, order, and publicly post factual fragments and coordinate their narrative construction.
preconditions: Victims aggregate public posts, while message-level truth checks cannot reject individually factual fragments.
mechanism: Open-channel cognitive collusion through generative montage.
interaction_surface: Public multi-agent information channel; aggregation; provenance and cross-message context.
primary_system_failure: F4 collective decision or belief integrity failure.
reported_impact: Downstream propagation of a fabricated conclusion.
metric_definition: Victim attack success and downstream deception rate.
unit_denominator: Unit: Rumor-event case or victim/judge decision.; Denominator: CoPHEME cases used in each evaluated split.
evidence_locators: Secs. 1 and 3, PDF pp. 1 to 6 for threat and method; Sec. 4, PDF pp. 6 to 8 for CoPHEME; Sec. 5, PDF pp. 8 to 12 for main result and propagation tables.

adversary_position: Remote black-box API user.
adversary_capabilities: Submits crafted queries and observes final outputs only.
preconditions: Internal agents may reveal, propagate, or retain proprietary information through orchestration.
mechanism: Worm-inspired black-box elicitation and cross-agent disclosure propagation.
interaction_surface: Public API; internal cross-agent communication; final output; architecture metadata.
primary_system_failure: F2 cross-principal or system-IP confidentiality violation.
reported_impact: Extraction of prompts, instructions, tools, agent count, and topology.
metric_definition: F1 for agent count, semantic or substring match for prompts and instructions, binary tool hit, graph-edit similarity for topology, and an extraction-rate aggregate over seven components.
unit_denominator: Unit: Application and protected component.; Denominator: Components or applications relevant to each metric. The aggregate ER is an average of seven component measures, not one universal ASR.
evidence_locators: Official USENIX record and arXiv full paper; abstract for black-box model and corpus size; method and metric sections for the seven measures; main tables for 87% and 92% results.

adversary_position: External content adversary without insider implementation knowledge.
adversary_capabilities: Place indirect prompt injection in public data; wait for privileged user query; receive exfiltrated email.
preconditions: Orchestrator delegates to distinct SQL/data and notification agents; poisoned record is retrieved; per-agent access controls allow split capabilities.
mechanism: Indirect prompt injection followed by orchestrator-mediated delegated authority composition and exfiltration.
interaction_surface: Public data; data-agent context; orchestrator planning; notification tool/email boundary.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and delegation/authorization integrity failure.
reported_impact: Exact sensitive records delivered to attacker-specified email in synthetic enterprise workflow.
metric_definition: Strict exact-match end-to-end attack success plus benign task correctness.
