unit_denominator: Workflow attack instances/queries; success requires correct sensitive content at correct attacker recipient, so partial or wrong-recipient cases are failures.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Abstract p. 1; Sec. 4.1 pp. 3-4 Figs. 2-3; Sec. 4.2 p. 4 Fig. 4; Sec. 5 pp. 4-7 Tables 1-5.

adversary_position: External adversary who plants content in a source later retrieved by a victim workflow.
adversary_capabilities: Publishes indirect prompts and relies on installed benign tools to ingest content, collect private data, and disclose it.
preconditions: The host lets untrusted retrieved instructions influence later privileged calls and does not enforce least privilege across the tool chain.
mechanism: Parasitic ingestion, private-data collection, and disclosure through composition of legitimate tools.
interaction_surface: External content; MCP servers and tools; cross-tool execution flow; host authorization.
primary_system_failure: F6 least-privilege and authority integrity failure.
reported_impact: F2 confidentiality loss through exfiltration.
metric_definition: Capability-gadget prevalence and separately measured end-to-end attack success.
unit_denominator: Unit: Tool, server, or end-to-end exploit chain.; Denominator: 12,230 tools and 1,360 servers for the census; separate trial denominators for demonstrations.
evidence_locators: Abstract and attack workflow, PDF p. 1 onward; attack stages in Secs. 2 to 3; census methods and tables; result tables for 1,062 tools and 370 servers; final IEEE metadata record.

adversary_position: external or contextual injector targeting planner-facing or executor-facing input
adversary_capabilities: insert role-specific malicious instructions and influence shared memory/context
preconditions: separable planner and executor roles, instrumentable memory, and outcome oracle
mechanism: prompt injection corrupts plan formation or action execution depending on role position
interaction_surface: planner input; planner-executor message; executor input; memory; tool execution
primary_system_failure: delegated plan and action integrity failure
reported_impact: role-dependent attack success and a utility-robustness trade-off
metric_definition: task utility and role-specific attack/robustness outcomes; exact paper terminology should be preserved
unit_denominator: task-run under role/attack/memory condition
evidence_locators: Findings EACL Abstract, sections 3-4, Figure 1, main tables, pp. 4547-4567

adversary_position: External or contextual source inducing credential propagation; leakage can also be accidental.
adversary_capabilities: Place or elicit credential fragments in shared context so downstream agents reproduce them under multiple pressure levels.
preconditions: Generated tokens, logits/entropy and 16 lexical/structural/information-theoretic/behavioral/contextual signals are observable during decoding; intervention can mask or stop generation.
mechanism: Sequential token-level risk accumulation with green/yellow/red zones and pre-completion stopping/masking.
interaction_surface: Shared context; downstream generation; token stream; inter-agent message boundary.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality failure through propagation amplification.
reported_impact: On the authors’ 2,000-task benchmark: F1 0.832, precision 1.000, recall 0.712, 0.0% observed task-level leakage, and utility 0.893.
metric_definition: Detection precision/recall/F1, task-level leak rate, output utility, latency, and risk-warning timing.
unit_denominator: 2,000 tasks across 13 attack categories and three pressure levels; task-level leak rate is not token-level detection rate.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract lines for four-agent pipeline, 2,000 tasks, 13 categories, three pressure levels, all headline metrics; full paper Secs. 3–5 for 16-signal model and baselines.

adversary_position: External content adversary placing one payload in an email, PDF, or webpage.
adversary_capabilities: Indirectly hijack first reader; embed role-specific malicious subtasks/data; instruct each recipient to reproduce payload downstream.
preconditions: Agents follow untrusted instructions and propagate text through global or predecessor-local histories; downstream role/tool capabilities are available.
mechanism: Self-replicating LLM-to-LLM prompt injection with role-conditioned payload and data carriage.
interaction_surface: External content; inter-agent messages; message history; retrieval/memory; role/tool boundaries.
primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Population infection plus scenario-specific confidentiality, content-integrity, scam, malware, and action impacts.
metric_definition: Scenario-specific attack success, infected count/fraction over turns, time to full infection, and defense ASR.
unit_denominator: Metrics change by experiment: workflow instructions/runs versus agents/population/turns. They must not be merged into one generic ASR.
evidence_locators: ArXiv/Springer technical text Sec. 3 pp. 3-4 Fig. 1; Sec. 4.1 p. 5 Fig. 4; Sec. 4.2 pp. 6-7 Fig. 6; Sec. 6 pp. 8-9 Table 2/Fig. 7.

adversary_position: compromised member agents in a decentralized ambient-agent population
adversary_capabilities: manipulate local behavior and inter-agent control flow; produce anomalous contributions
preconditions: decentralized peers exchange trust evidence through gossip; local monitors and federated adaptation remain available; enough honest evidence dominates
mechanism: compromised behavior propagates or influences peers; defense fuses local MAPE-K/DCA anomaly signals, probabilistic trust, gossip, federated learning, and encrypted aggregation
interaction_surface: agent-local behavior; peer communication; distributed trust evidence; control flow
primary_system_failure: distributed collaboration integrity and resilience failure
reported_impact: malicious-agent acceptance, control-flow hijacking, degraded collaboration, and loss of continued operation
metric_definition: malicious-agent identification, control-flow hijack rate, recovery/resilience, and collaborative performance; metric formulas require final PDF verification
unit_denominator: agent/event/task-level denominators are not fully specified in the note; do not compare headline rates until tables are signed off
evidence_locators: Official AAAI abstract and metadata; repository note method pp.2-5 and evaluation pp.6-7, but exact table/figure locators require author signoff

adversary_position: Byzantine or faulty member agents repeatedly supplying a prescribed incorrect candidate answer.
adversary_capabilities: Send protocol-valid wrong answers through normal graph edges.
preconditions: Seven-node fixed graphs, trusted experiment controller and aggregation, and confidence probes used by CP-WBFT.
mechanism: Faulty-answer propagation and confidence-weighted voting.
interaction_surface: Member messages; topology; collective aggregation.
primary_system_failure: F4 collective task-decision integrity failure.
reported_impact: Wrong mathematical answer or unsafe classification.
metric_definition: Task accuracy and reported reliability accuracy.
unit_denominator: Unit: Task instance under a fault configuration.; Denominator: GSM8K or XSTest examples in each experiment.
evidence_locators: Pilot experiment, PDF pp. 2 to 3, Table 1 and Fig. 2; datasets and metrics, PDF pp. 2 and 5; method, PDF pp. 3 to 5 and Fig. 3; experimental setting, PDF p. 5 and Fig. 2/Table 2; result tables, PDF pp. 5 to 7.

adversary_position: scenario-dependent malicious, self-interested, or faulty member
adversary_capabilities: configured through roles, incentives, protocols, topology, and environment conditions
preconditions: controlled scenario oracle, full trajectory logging, and explicit experiment quintuple
mechanism: scenario modules induce or reveal interaction-dependent collusion, resource overreach, semantic drift, or strategic misreporting
interaction_surface: topology; protocol; incentives; agent roles; environment; task
primary_system_failure: mixed collective integrity, resource control, and reliability failures
reported_impact: trajectory-grounded risk signals vary under independently configurable structural conditions
metric_definition: risk-specific trajectory-grounded measures plus task outcomes
unit_denominator: scenario/trajectory/module dependent; no single universal denominator
evidence_locators: ACL demo Abstract, sections 2-4, Figure 1, pp. 167-177

adversary_position: malicious member agent sending harmful protocol-valid messages
adversary_capabilities: transmit messages whose downstream state effects appear plausible
preconditions: defender observes graph, recent state, and candidate message; learned simulator approximates benign state transitions
mechanism: counterfactual simulation predicts local/global state change and intercepts messages whose reconstruction deviates from benign dynamics
interaction_surface: inter-agent messages; propagation paths; communication state
primary_system_failure: collective decision-integrity and propagation-containment failure
reported_impact: harmful state changes and degraded collective answers
metric_definition: accuracy, ASR, precision, recall, F1, and cost; definitions are paper-specific
unit_denominator: task/run and message-detection units; do not combine ASR with agent-fraction metrics
evidence_locators: Repository note sections 3-4 pp.3-7 and section 5 pp.8-11; arXiv full text must be signed off for exact tables

adversary_position: malicious agent, server, tool, intermediary, or external attacker depending on protocol lifecycle
adversary_capabilities: spoof, tamper, replay, abuse discovery, escalate privilege, disclose data, or deny service
preconditions: protocol specifications/implementations expose modeled lifecycle states; MCP case assumes multi-server resolver policies
mechanism: protocol lifecycle and trust-assumption weaknesses break identity, integrity, authorization, or availability
interaction_surface: discovery; authentication; session establishment; messages; delegation; tools; update lifecycle
primary_system_failure: protocol identity, authorization, integrity, confidentiality, and availability failure
reported_impact: qualitative twelve-risk matrix plus empirical wrong-provider tool execution in MCP composition
metric_definition: qualitative likelihood/impact/overall risk; case-study wrong-provider execution rate
unit_denominator: protocol/risk item and MCP resolution trial; exact empirical denominator requires table-level signoff
evidence_locators: arXiv Abstract; protocol architecture and comparison sections; twelve-risk tables; MCP measurement case study

adversary_position: Malicious user submitting one crafted but superficially legitimate request.
adversary_capabilities: Choose initial request only; no later interaction or direct component compromise.
preconditions: Orchestrator autonomously decomposes work; local safety classifiers see subtasks but not the complete plan/data dependencies.
mechanism: Semantic Intent Fragmentation across locally benign subtasks.
interaction_surface: Orchestrator decomposition; local subtask guardrails; plan/data-flow boundary.
primary_system_failure: Compositional authorization and information-flow/action-integrity failure.
reported_impact: 10 of 14 generated scenarios produced policy-violating plans while all component tasks passed local checks; defense detects all confirmed cases in the same small study.
metric_definition: Scenario-level attack success, local-classifier pass rate, and defense false-positive/detection outcomes.
unit_denominator: 14 generated enterprise scenarios: 10/14 = 71.4%; six classifier families are not the denominator for attack success.
evidence_locators: Published/arXiv Abstract p. 1; threat/model sections; evaluation result reporting 10/14; publisher metadata for Vol. 9 No. 1 pp. 229–237.

adversary_position: malicious participant agents in decentralized debate
adversary_capabilities: send manipulative messages through legitimate peer channels
preconditions: agents have persistent neighbor identities and local histories; contrastive training attacks represent deployment attacks; enough honest connectivity survives pruning
mechanism: credit-based local detector ranks neighbors and removes bottom-k peers to suppress malicious communication
interaction_surface: peer messages; local neighbor topology; member influence
primary_system_failure: collective decision-integrity failure
reported_impact: malicious-agent influence, degraded group accuracy, and communication contamination
metric_definition: malicious-agent detection rate, task accuracy recovery, and rounds to detection
unit_denominator: agent detection events and system task instances; near-100% detection is a highlighted setting, not universal
evidence_locators: Official ACM abstract and pages 3135-3146; repository note method section 4 pp.4-7 and results section 5 pp.7-10

adversary_position: Malicious user or compromised member/role agent.
adversary_capabilities: Mix malicious functionality into benign requirements or modify selected design, coding, or testing role profiles.
preconditions: Role-separated software MAS; cross-stage artifacts are trusted by downstream agents; generated programs are run in a sandbox.
mechanism: Implicit malicious behavior injection through requirements or compromised role profiles, propagated across development stages.
interaction_surface: User requirements; role prompts; shared code/design/test artifacts.
primary_system_failure: Compositional software action and artifact-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Executable software retains benign utility while implementing malicious operations.
metric_definition: Benign utility, utility under attack, consistency, refusal rate, ASR, and defense-adjusted ASR/refusal.
unit_denominator: Software requirement/task instances; ASR concerns malicious functionality in generated software, not compromised-agent count.
evidence_locators: PDF Methodology pp. 3-5 and Fig. 2; Experiment p. 5; attack/defense results pp. 6-8, Figs. 4-5.

adversary_position: One or more malicious peer agents.
adversary_capabilities: Provide incorrect recommendations and manipulate coalition size, apparent expertise, message length/order, dominance, and rhetoric.
preconditions: Representative-agent aggregation architecture; peers are presented as decision evidence; objective-answer tasks.
mechanism: Conformity pressure, expertise signaling, dominant-speaker effects, and rhetorical persuasion.
interaction_surface: Peer-message content; group composition; aggregation context.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Representative accuracy and willingness to retain the correct answer decline under stronger social pressure.
metric_definition: Representative-agent accuracy and decision-change/adoption rates.
unit_denominator: Question instances under each controlled condition.
evidence_locators: PDF study design Sec. 3 pp. 3-5; experiments Secs. 4-5 pp. 4-15 and main tables/figures; limitations section.

adversary_position: malicious user or external content source; scenario-dependent impersonator/tool attacker
adversary_capabilities: direct/indirect prompt injection, impersonation, information theft, malicious code execution, and denial of service through benchmark interfaces
preconditions: AutoGen/CrewAI configurations, scenario tool environment, benchmark-defined attack access, and task evaluators
mechanism: scenario-specific adversarial instructions exploit routing, authority, identity, and tool trust
interaction_surface: user prompt; external content; identities; tool interface; inter-agent workflow
primary_system_failure: workflow confidentiality, action integrity, and availability failure
reported_impact: attack success and benign task effectiveness vary materially by model and interaction configuration
metric_definition: Attack Success Rate, Task Success Rate, and Effective Robustness Score combining resistance and effectiveness
unit_denominator: 300 adversarial instances and 100 harmless tasks across five domains/six attack types; ERS is benchmark-specific
evidence_locators: ACL Abstract, section 5/5.1, Table 3 and results tables, pp. 31238-31268

adversary_position: Peer/requester agent operating through normal inter-agent channels; scenarios include ordinary, emergent, and overtly malicious requests.
adversary_capabilities: Issue contextually plausible requests and exploit elevated trust; no weight, orchestration, or infrastructure compromise.
preconditions: Parameterized trust changes disclosure behavior; Minimum Necessary Information labels are treated as the authorization reference.
mechanism: Trust-conditioned over-exposure: increased trust weakens cross-role information gates and permits requests beyond the MNI baseline.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent requests; trust policy; cross-role information boundary; optional guardian.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and authorization-boundary failure.
reported_impact: Disclosure beyond the MNI reference and trust-sensitive authorization drift in synthetic scenario chains.
metric_definition: Task success, Over-Exposure Rate (MNI boundary violations), and Authorization Drift (sensitivity/slope across trust levels).
unit_denominator: Interaction-chain and disclosure-opportunity level as defined by the scenario/MNI labels; do not treat OER or AD as ordinary ASR.
evidence_locators: ArXiv full text Sec. 3 pp. 3-4 Eqs. 2-4; Sec. 4 pp. 4-5 Tables I-III; Sec. 5 pp. 6-10 Figs. 4-9.

adversary_position: Operator or prompt attacker controlling one member’s system prompt.
adversary_capabilities: Seed a three-digit subliminal token preference; no weight access or verbatim payload forwarding.
preconditions: Agents relay semantic summaries/responses through a chain; downstream models can acquire latent preference from outputs.
mechanism: Subliminal prompting and semantic preference propagation without explicit malicious string repetition.
interaction_surface: One member’s system prompt; ordinary inter-agent semantic messages; downstream behavioral distribution.
primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation/collective value or truthfulness integrity degradation.
reported_impact: Elevated target-concept preference over hops and reduced TruthfulQA accuracy/log probability for selected tokens.
metric_definition: Target response rate, target log probability, fold increase, and TruthfulQA accuracy/log probability.
unit_denominator: Agent-hop/question/model observations; fold change is not an infection rate and should not be compared to ASR.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v1 Abstract p. 1; Sec. 3 pp. 4-5 Figs. 2-3; Sec. 4 pp. 5-8 Tables 1-2; discussion pp. 8-9.

adversary_position: One malicious member agent targeting one private-memory holder.
adversary_capabilities: Participates in normal communication, solicits private data, observes topology-permitted messages, and accumulates information across rounds.
preconditions: Static known graph, one attacker and one target, synchronous text communication, synthetic PII.
mechanism: Repeated cooperative-looking solicitation and topology-mediated relay of private cues.
interaction_surface: Private memory; inter-agent messages; topology; role placement.
primary_system_failure: F2 cross-principal confidentiality violation.
reported_impact: Recovery and diffusion of private PII by an unauthorized participant.
metric_definition: Exact-match-plus-LLM-inference leakage rate, ever-leaked entities, and temporal diffusion.
unit_denominator: Unit: PII entity and trace or configuration.; Denominator: Seeded protected PII entities or evaluated traces, as defined by each result.
evidence_locators: Secs. 3.1 to 3.3, PDF pp. 3 to 6 and Fig. 1/Table 1 for state, roles, and six topologies; Sec. 4, PDF pp. 7 to 9, Tables 2 to 3 and Figs. 2 to 3 for leakage and temporal results; limitations, PDF p. 9.

adversary_position: malicious member agents injecting misinformation
adversary_capabilities: send persuasive malicious messages along allowed edges
preconditions: global temporal graph and messages are visible; defender can prune edges and isolate communities
mechanism: spatio-temporal GNN estimates node risk entropy and edge attack conductivity, followed by edge correction/pruning and community isolation
interaction_surface: inter-agent messages; temporal graph; communities
primary_system_failure: propagation containment and collective decision-integrity failure
reported_impact: toxicity/malicious influence spreads and group utility degrades
metric_definition: toxicity or attack impact, task success/utility, suppression efficiency, and scalability
unit_denominator: task/run and graph condition; 58% reduction and >90% utility refer to highlighted GPT-4o setting
evidence_locators: ACL Anthology abstract lines 58-61; metadata lines 62-99; repository note method pp.3-6 and results pp.7-10

adversary_position: One low-privilege malicious member agent.
adversary_capabilities: Submit and advocate an attacker-controlled URL; choose homoglyph, subdomain, path, parameter, IP, and other structural representations; no architecture/defense knowledge assumed.
preconditions: Attacker controls a domain and has an allowed recommendation channel; downstream agents/auditor use URL and context to decide.
mechanism: URL-structure deception propagated through recommendation, review, debate, or voting.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent recommendation messages; URL representation; web/tool boundary; collective aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective recommendation and decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Final auditor accepts/recommends a malicious destination; phishing/malware/prompt-injection consequences are potential, not directly executed.
metric_definition: ASR is fraction of repeated runs in which the final auditor does not classify the URL as high risk; ten repetitions per configuration.
unit_denominator: Run/configuration-level decisions, not agent or population compromise.

adversary_position: Coalition of malicious member agents in a simulated social platform.
adversary_capabilities: Post, comment, privately message, coordinate, cultivate victims, and adapt to warnings/monitoring.
preconditions: Simulator permits public/private communication and simulated transfers; malicious agents receive explicit fraud goals.
mechanism: Coordinated social persuasion and coalition reinforcement across the fraud lifecycle.
interaction_surface: Public posts/comments; private messages; membership; transfer decisions.
primary_system_failure: Collective manipulation and decision-integrity failure with simulated financial impact.
reported_impact: Victim engagement, migration to private conversation, and simulated transfers.
metric_definition: Separate population-level fraud success, conversation-level success, transfer/stage conversion, and collaboration-failure metrics.
unit_denominator: Populations, conversations, agents, or stage opportunities depending on metric; these must not be collapsed.
evidence_locators: Full text Sec. 3 pp. 3-5 and Fig. 2; Sec. 3.3 p. 5; Sec. 4.1 p. 6; Sec. 4.3 p. 8 Table 2; Sec. 5 pp. 11-13 Tables 9-10.

adversary_position: Malicious member inside an otherwise cooperative debate group.
adversary_capabilities: Read full debate history; promote a designated target; generate multi-layer arguments, rebuttals, fused narratives, Best-of-N candidates, and RAG-supported rhetoric.
preconditions: All participants consume a shared transcript; a final decision is produced by debate/majority; the controlled evaluation assigns a wrong target for reproducible measurement.
mechanism: Inference-time adaptive persuasion and contextual accumulation, optionally strengthened by RAG and Best-of-N selection.
interaction_surface: Peer messages; shared debate transcript; majority-vote aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Reduced group answer accuracy and increased agreement with the attacker-selected wrong answer; no real-world downstream action is executed.
metric_definition: Two-part outcome: drop in final group accuracy and rise in the fraction of agents agreeing with the adversarial target; paper also reports setting-specific accuracy/consensus changes.
unit_denominator: Question/debate-instance level for final accuracy plus agent-within-round agreement fractions; the headline 10–40% and >30% are ranges across evaluated settings, not one universal effect.
evidence_locators: Publisher HTML: abstract and Threat model & Attack design; paper pp. 4-5 Fig. 1/Algorithm 1; pp. 10-11 setup/metrics; pp. 14-16 Figs. 11-13 for mitigation.

adversary_position: One compromised member agent.
adversary_capabilities: Generate protocol-valid misinformation and adapt wording to mimic benign embeddings or disperse benign messages; cannot alter defense code.
preconditions: Embedding-based pruning/weighting; generation-time token confidence available for proposed defense.
mechanism: Slow Drift, Benign Wrapper, and Chaos Seeding evade text-embedding separation assumptions.
interaction_surface: Inter-agent messages; graph anomaly detector; aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision integrity and malicious-member attribution failure.
reported_impact: Embedding defenses retain malicious messages and group accuracy degrades; confidence filtering improves reported robustness.
metric_definition: Task accuracy/exact match, ASR, embedding distances, malicious-agent AUROC, signal half-life, and area under AUROC-by-round.
unit_denominator: Question/task instances for accuracy/ASR and agent/message labels for AUROC; signal persistence is round-indexed.
evidence_locators: Full text Sec. 5 pp. 4-5 Fig. 2; Sec. 6 pp. 5-6; Sec. 7.1 p. 6; Sec. 7.2 pp. 6-7 Tables 1/3; Sec. 8 pp. 7-8 Tables 4-5.

adversary_position: Cooperating sender and receiver endpoints facing a passive traffic observer or warden.
adversary_capabilities: Choose storage, timing, and behavioral events and share protocol state or keys.
preconditions: Shared keys or protocol state, available channel, and a passive observer without endpoint compromise.
mechanism: Pi-CCAP encodes encrypted payload bits across storage, timing, and behavioral event dimensions.
interaction_surface: Message content; event timing; behavioral metadata; global communication trace.
primary_system_failure: From a defender view, oversight or monitorability integrity. From a legitimate-user view, communication privacy is the protected property.
reported_impact: Potential covert coordination. The construction itself is dual-use.
metric_definition: Effective bits per round, total capacity, bit error or robustness, statistical AUC, and LLM-warden detection outcomes.
